output.summary: KEP-3104 introduces an optional, versioned `kuberc` file for client-side user preferences (command aliases and default options), separate from cluster credentials in kubeconfig, and deprecates the kubeconfig `Preferences` field. The KEP is in implementable status at stage beta.
output.rationale: kubectl has strong backwards-compatibility guarantees, so users need an opt-in place for new behaviors that could break existing scripts. The existing kubeconfig `preferences` field is underused because new clusters usually produce new kubeconfig files holding credentials, so a separate file keeps server config and user preferences apart and applies regardless of which `--kubeconfig` or `$KUBECONFIG` is used. Reviewers pushed to start simple with command aliases only and to keep builtin commands from being shadowed.

alternatives.option: Use XDG base directory locations for the new file
alternatives.why_not: Maintainers opted out because it would cause an awful partition across tooling that didn't upgrade client-go; a reviewer noted it is worth considering for a net-new file, and the KEP was asked to explicitly address and reject it.

alternatives.option: Keep using the existing kubeconfig `Preferences` field
alternatives.why_not: Creating a new cluster generally yields a new kubeconfig with credentials and host information, so the design wants a clear separation between server configuration and user preferences.

alternatives.option: Allow aliases for subcommands and flag or namespace aliasing from the start
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (soltysh) advised starting simple with just command aliases, and noted that aliases must not shadow builtin commands; git does not support such aliasing either.

alternatives.option: Opt out of deprecations for the kubeconfig field
alternatives.why_not: Per the later decision on PR #6350, the maintainers decided it is not wise to opt out of deprecations, so that functionality will not be supported.

evidence.quote: This proposal introduces an optional `kuberc` file that is used to separate cluster credentials and server configuration from user preferences.
users can split kubeconfig files into various locations, while maintaining a single preference file that will apply no matter which `--kubeconfig` flag or `$KUBECONFIG` env var is pointing to.
we need to ensure that builtin commands stay builtin commands, otherwise we'll introduce a new set of problems where users will start reporting problems
I don't want to go that far, I'd start simple with just command aliases.
We've decided it's not wise to opt-out of deprecations, so we're not going to support that functionality.
